name: McCormick standard spice jar (US)
notes: Converted from 1.8 in diameter x 4.5 in tall, incl. cap, as measured by a spice-rack maker; the same site elsewhere lists McCormick/Spice Islands as 4-3/8 in x 1-3/4 in. McCormick publishes no jar drawing, so allow a few mm.

name: Simply Organic spice bottle (standard glass)
notes: Retailer FAQ: 4.45 x 1.97 x 1.97 in (allspice 2.57 oz). Other retailer listings for different spices give ~4.5 in tall x 1.95 in. Square-ish footprint; no official drawing found.

name: 4 oz square glass spice jar, 43 mm cap (Specialty Bottle HBSQ4B)
notes: Specialty Bottle lists 1.7 in wide x 4.2 in tall with a 43/400 lid and shaker; it does not say if height includes the lid or if width is across the flats. TricorBraun/Container & Packaging 43-485 versions list 4.09 in total height and 1.71 in.

name: Crown cap (beer bottle cap), 26 mm pry-off
notes: Tapon Corona 26 mm pry-off datasheet: OD 1.262 +/-0.012 in, ID 1.055 +/-0.005 in, height 0.236 +/-0.005 in, panel 0.016 in, 21 corrugations. EN 17177 is the '26 mm diameter, 6 mm height' crown-cap standard. The bottle finish lip OD (ISO 12821 tall / ISO 12822 shallow 26 mm crown finish) is paywalled, so it is not included.

name: US 12 oz longneck beer bottle (ISB, 355 ml)
notes: Listed as 9.09 in (23.1 cm) tall x 2.4 in (6.1 cm) diameter. Homebrew vendors round the height to 9 in. Takes a 26 mm crown cap.

name: PCO 1881 28 mm PET soda bottle neck finish
notes: The 28 mm nominal thread is measured at its widest point, with the neck support ring just below it. The ISBT drawing 3784253-21 (PCO 1881-1) has exact T/E/ring values, but it could not be machine-read, so the thread OD, cap OD and cap height are omitted. Caps use a 2-start thread.

name: 2 litre PET soda bottle
notes: Typical bottle 4.33 in (11 cm) diameter x 12.4 in (31.5 cm) tall, per dimensions.com. Wikipedia gives the typical range of 100-120 mm diameter and 300-330 mm height. Shape varies by bottler. US bottles normally use a 28 mm PCO 1881 neck.

name: Standard 12 oz / 355 ml beverage can (211 x 413)
notes: Crown Holdings spec: body diameter 66 mm (211 code), height 122.22 mm (413 code). The lid/end is necked down to a smaller diameter (202 end), which is not given here.

name: Sleek/slim 12 oz / 355 ml beverage can (Crown CrownSleek)
notes: Crown spec: diameter 58 mm (204.5 code), height 156.59 mm (602 code). Other makers' sleek cans are similar but not identical.

name: Ball regular mouth mason jar (70 mm) + 16 oz pint jar
notes: A Ball Team Q&A answer on Target gives 70 mm (2.756 in) for regular mouth lids/jars. TricorBraun lists the regular-mouth finish as 70-450 (thread pitch not published). Pint jar (Ball 61000) from WebstaurantStore: 5-1/8 in tall, 3-1/8 in max dia, 2-3/4 in top, 2-1/4 in bottom; the 473 ml volume is a 16 US fl oz conversion.

name: Ball wide mouth mason jar (86 mm)
notes: 86 mm Ball wide-mouth lids (Berlin Packaging 6788C07). TricorBraun lists wide-mouth canning jar finishes as 86-400; the thread pitch is not published. WebstaurantStore's wide-mouth pint listing (Ball 66000ZFP) is self-inconsistent (top dia larger than max dia, 6-13/16 in tall), so jar dims are omitted.

name: Nalgene 32 oz Wide Mouth bottle
notes: Nalgene specs: 8.25 in (21 cm) tall incl. cap, 3.5 in (89 mm) dia, 63 mm cap, 6.25 oz. The 946 ml volume is a 32 US fl oz conversion. The 63 mm cap also fits the 48 oz wide mouth.

name: Hydro Flask 32 oz Wide Mouth bottle
notes: evo listing (current refresh): 3.58 in dia, 9.4 in tall with Flex Cap, 2.26 in mouth, 15.2 oz. The older version is listed at 3.56 in / 9.1 in / 2.28 in mouth, and straw-lid versions run 10.1-10.2 in tall. hydroflask.com blocked fetching.

name: Bicycle handlebar clamp and grip diameters
notes: Sheldon Brown: 25.4 is ISO, 26.0 is Italian, 31.8 is road oversize; 22.2 is the flat-bar grip and 23.8 the drop-bar grip. BikeGremlin adds 35 mm (Easton-originated MTB) and notes 31.8 is also used on flat bars.

name: Bicycle seatpost and seat-collar diameters
notes: Post sizes: Sheldon Brown lists 27.2, 30.9 and 31.6 as common, and BikeRadar adds 34.9 for droppers. Collar sizes match the frame seat-tube OD, not the post (e.g. 31.6 post -> 34.9 collar); the collar list is from Wolf Tooth's range on VitalMTB.

name: Bicycle bottle cage bosses
notes: Two M5 x 0.8 threaded bosses 64 mm (2.5 in) apart center-to-center. Some fork/downtube mounts add a third hole at the same pitch. No ISO reference was cited by the source.

name: Bicycle fork steerer tube diameters
notes: Sheldon Brown headset crib sheet. A tapered steerer is 1-1/8 (28.6) at the stem and 1.5 in (38.1) at the crown. Many tapered crown-race seats are actually ~39.8-40 mm (Park CRC-15 / Trek specs, from search snippets only), so check the specific fork.

name: Tripod screw 1/4-20 UNC (ISO 1222)
notes: Basic UNC values from eFunda (major 0.2500, pitch dia 0.2175, minor 0.1905/0.1959 in). Little Machine Shop gives tap drill #7 = 0.201 in (75% thread) and clearance F/H. A 5.1 mm metric drill is a near substitute. Some tripod-thread pages quote 5.35 mm as the 'core hole', which is larger than standard.

name: Tripod screw 3/8-16 UNC (ISO 1222)
notes: Basic UNC values from eFunda (major 0.3750, pitch dia 0.3344, minor 0.3005/0.3073 in). Little Machine Shop gives tap drill 5/16 in = 0.3125 in and clearance W/X. Used for tripod-to-head and pro-camera mounts.

name: Arca-Swiss style quick-release plate dovetail
notes: No official standard exists. Acratech gives 38 mm (1.5 in) width and a 45 deg dovetail, and RRS gives a ~35 mm base and 45 deg. Measured plates range from 38.0 to 38.75 mm (astropix). Thickness and length are from one example plate (Leofoto PL-62: 62 x 38 x 10 mm).
